## Adjudication
Sided with Codex. I traced the production failover on a SECOND poll and confirmed the bug is real, not a phantom. On the persistence-failure path the authoritative `write_handle_sidecar(runpod_handle)` raises (the test's `_raising_write`), the best-effort `on_launched` write is swallowed by the router, so the sidecar STILL holds the GCP handle. On the next tick `read_handle_sidecar` returns that unchanged GCP handle, `_is_gcp_async_workload_failure(handle, result)` (`backend_poll.py:202-206`) returns True again (still backend=="gcp", status=="dead", phase=="terminal_workload_failed" — nothing changed), the dispatch block at `backend_poll.py:504-507` re-enters `_failover_dead_gcp_to_runpod`, and `backend_poll.py:306` calls `failover_to_runpod_after_async_workload_crash(...)` a SECOND time — a second paid RunPod launch. There is NO durable failure-sentinel / lease check anywhere between line 504 and line 306 to block the repeat. The code's own comment at `backend_poll.py:336-343` names this exact failure mode ("the next tick would re-read a GCP handle ... and fire a SECOND RunPod launch — breaching 'exactly once'"); the persistence guard it added only prevents emitting `running`, NOT the re-launch when persistence itself fails. The committed test ENCODES the bug: the docstring at `tests/test_backend_poll.py:210-212` says the second poll "does NOT fire a second RunPod launch," but the assertion at line 262 is `len(rp.launches) <= launches_after_first + 1` — with `launches_after_first == 1`, that is `2 <= 2`, which PERMITS exactly the second launch the docstring claims to forbid. Docstring and assertion are mutually contradictory. Claude's two-line minor note reframed this as "bounded per-tick … acceptable," but "bounded per-tick" is a strictly weaker invariant than the plan/MF4's "exactly once" and the helper's own docstring (`backend_poll.py:279, 497-498`); the code satisfies the weaker one and violates the stated one. The leak IS bounded (one extra pod): `sidecar_persistence_failed` is NOT in `TRANSIENT_CAPACITY_REASONS` (only `no_compute_available` is — `autonomous_session_watch.py:6179`), so the watcher parks at `blocked` and never re-drives — but the double-poll-before-park is the NORMAL case (the bg-Bash poll loop re-polls on the JSON's `next_interval` well before the 10-min watcher parks), not a rare race, so the second paid RunPod launch is expected behavior on this path, not an edge case. Step 5c-bis does not apply (tag is `substantive`, not `marker-shape`/`smoke-run-missing`). Real & blocking → FAIL.

## Findings carried forward
- **[BLOCKER, substantive] async-runpod-failover-persistence-repeat** (Codex). The MF4 persistence-failure path launches a SECOND RunPod on the next poll of the still-GCP sidecar, breaching the plan's "exactly once" invariant and burning paid RunPod capacity. Root cause: no durable failover-already-attempted guard before `backend_poll.py:306`; the persistence guard only gates emitting `running`, not the re-entry into the launch. Fix (either): (a) persist a failure-sentinel / lease before returning `sidecar_persistence_failed`, then short-circuit `_failover_dead_gcp_to_runpod` to re-emit the terminal infra JSON WITHOUT launching when the sentinel/lease for this issue already exists; OR (b) check the existing RunPod lease/marker at entry and return the terminal infra JSON without re-launching. AND tighten the test to `assert len(rp.launches) == launches_after_first` after the second poll (the current `<= +1` is the contradiction that lets the bug land), and fix the docstring to match.
